title: Stale namespace cache causes intermittent privilege denial for API keys in Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent 403/authorization failures for otherwise valid API keys. Failures began after a control-plane rollout that changed how namespace-to-org bindings are cached on edge nodes. This ticket tracks diagnosis, mitigation, fix, and rollout plan.

Observed behavior: Requests authenticated with API keys occasionally receive 403 with 'organization scope mismatch' or 'insufficient scope' logs. Failures are transient — retrying within seconds usually succeeds. Impact has been seen in Hosted-connected Dedicated clusters and some Private installations that opted into the new cache mode.

Initial customer reports: On-call received multiple escalations (Customer A, Customer B) showing production errors and user-facing outages in critical paths (billing webhooks and embeddings pipelines). Customers experienced 1-3% request failure spikes lasting 30s-5m scattered across regions.
reproduction_steps: Deploy current control-plane build with cache-mode=sticky on a Dedicated node pool and warm auth cache by making API calls across 10 orgs.
Trigger a rolling restart of the auth service (control-plane) and observe edge nodes accepting rotated apikey metadata via the fanout channel.
Send parallel requests using recently rotated API keys while the cache invalidation window overlaps kv-sync; some requests return 403 with 'org-scope mismatch' in edge logs.
root_cause_summary: Race between cache eviction and namespace affinity reconciliation. When control-plane updates mapping during rotation, edge nodes sometimes apply a partial update that leaves the namespace->org binding stale for short windows. The sticky cache fast path skipped full reconciliation for performance, and our consistency guard only applied on startup, not on in-flight mapping deltas. This produced intermittent authorization misbinding for keys whose tenant affinity changed within the reconciliation window.
mitigation: Hotfix: fall back to conservative reconciliation for affected node pool by setting CACHE_MODE=consistent; deploy a rolling restart of edge sync agents to clear partial states. Short-term configuration rolled to Dedicated customers where the incidents were observed. Alert added to detect >0.5% 403 rate over rolling 1m windows per cluster.
proposed_fix: 1) Update edge sync logic to apply per-namespace versioned deltas and verify full mapping before accepting tokens. 2) Add a reconciliation acknowledgment RPC so control-plane knows when an edge node has applied the mapping. 3) Tighten tests around concurrent map updates and token validation. Implementation will include unit tests, integration test with simulated fanout delays, and a canary rollout.
rollout_plan: Patch runtime-1.24 with the fix, publish canary to a single Dedicated cluster, monitor 403/error rates and latency, then expand to remaining Dedicated pools and Private installer releases. Provide a config flag to opt into sticky mode after sufficient validation. Targeting gradual rollout over 7 days with rollback plan to set CACHE_MODE=consistent if errors increase.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for map delta application and version checks
Integration test simulating stale-delta fanout and asserting no 403s for in-flight requests
Chaos test: delayed fanout and agent restart during key rotation
Synthetic traffic monitoring dashboard: track per-key 403 spikes and reconciliation latencies
